digest.component_or_area: LLM model class configuration and resolution
propositions: Rebar lacks structured configuration to express model selection per capability tier (frontier/standard/trivial), forcing per-pass inference instead of declarative wiring.

The new schema defines three config slots (frontier, standard, trivial) accepting model, provider, endpoint, and optional fallback array; all are parsed and validated but fallback consumption is deferred to a sibling task.
Secrets boundary is enforced: api_key is forbidden in both class slots and fallback entries; configuration of secrets is environment-only via REBAR_LLM_* vars not config file keys.

When a slot is unset, it resolves to the documented per-class default (frontier→claude-opus-4-8, standard→claude-sonnet-4-6, trivial→claude-haiku-4-5), preserving byte-identical behavior to the current release.

The fallback sub-object schema is non-recursive (nested fallback entries are rejected) with model required, provider and endpoint optional (inferred/defaulted if omitted), and api_key forbidden; empty fallback array and absent fallback key are equivalent.

Environment variables address nested slots by field (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL, REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_PROVIDER, etc.), maintaining per-key precedence (CLI > env > config file > default) without object-level merge rules.
